ayahs.textEnglish: Nun. CONSIDER the pen, and all that they write [therewith]!
Thou art not, by thy Sustainer's grace, a madman!

ayahs.textLatin: Wa inna laka la'ajran gaira mamnūn(in).
ayahs.textEnglish: And, verily, thine shall be a reward neverending –
for, behold, thou keepest indeed to a sublime way of life;
and [one day] thou shalt see, and they [who now deride thee] shall see,
which of you was bereft of reason.

ayahs.textArabic: اِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ اَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيْلِهٖۖ وَهُوَ اَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِيْنَ
ayahs.textLatin: Inna rabbaka huwa a‘lamu biman ḍalla ‘an sabīlih(ī), wa huwa a‘lamu bil-muhtadīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: Verily, thy Sustainer alone is fully aware as to who has strayed from His path, Just as He alone is fully aware of those who have found the right way.
Hence, defer not to [the likes and dislikes of] those who give the lie to the truth:
they would like thee to be soft [with them], so that they might be soft [with thee].

ayahs.textLatin: Wa lā tuṭi‘ kulla ḥallāfim mahīn(in).
ayahs.textEnglish: Furthermore, defer not to the contemptible swearer of oaths,
[or to] the slanderer that goes about with defaming tales,
[or] the withholder of good, [or] the sinful aggressor,
[or] one who is cruel, by greed possessed, and, in addition to all this, utterly useless [to his fellow-men].

ayahs.textLatin: An kāna żā māliw wa banīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: Is it because he is possessed of worldly goods and children

ayahs.textArabic: اِذَا تُتْلٰى عَلَيْهِ اٰيٰتُنَا قَالَ اَسَاطِيْرُ الْاَوَّلِيْنَۗ
ayahs.textEnglish: that, whenever Our messages are conveyed to him, such a one says, "Fables of ancient times"?
[For this] We shall brand him with indelible disgrace!

ayahs.textArabic: اِنَّا بَلَوْنٰهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَآ اَصْحٰبَ الْجَنَّةِۚ اِذْ اَقْسَمُوْا لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِيْنَۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Innā balaunāhum kamā balaunā aṣḥābal-jannah(ti), iż aqsamū layaṣrimunnahā muṣbiḥīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: [As for such sinners,] behold, We [but] try them as We tried the owners of a certain garden who vowed that they would surely harvest its fruit on the morrow,
and made no allowance [for the will of God]:

ayahs.textArabic: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَاۤىِٕفٌ مِّنْ رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَاۤىِٕمُوْنَ
ayahs.textLatin: Fa ṭāfa ‘alaihā ṭā'ifum mir rabbika wa hum nā'imūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: whereupon a visitation for thy Sustainer came upon that [garden] while they were asleep,
so that by the morrow it became barren and bleak.
Now when they rose at early morn, they called unto one another,

ayahs.textArabic: اَنِ اغْدُوْا عَلٰى حَرْثِكُمْ اِنْ كُنْتُمْ صٰرِمِيْنَ
ayahs.textEnglish: "Go early to your tilth if you want to harvest the fruit!"
Thus they launched forth, whispering unto one another,

ayahs.textArabic: اَنْ لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّسْكِيْنٌۙ
ayahs.textEnglish: "Indeed, no needy person shall enter it today [and come] upon you [unawares],"
– and early they went, strongly bent upon their purpose.
But as soon as they beheld [the garden and could not recognize] it, they exclaimed, "Surely we have lost our way!"
- [and then,] "Nay, but we have been rendered destitute!"

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ اَوْسَطُهُمْ اَلَمْ اَقُلْ لَّكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُوْنَ
ayahs.textLatin: Qāla ausaṭuhum alam aqul lakum lau lā tusabbiḥūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: Said the most right-minded among them: "Did I not tell you, 'Will you not extol God's limitless glory?’"

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُوْا سُبْحٰنَ رَبِّنَآ اِنَّا كُنَّا ظٰلِمِيْنَ
ayahs.textLatin: Qālū subḥāna rabbinā innā kunnā ẓālimīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: They answered: "Limitless in His glory is our Sustainer! Verily, we were doing wrong!"
- and then they turned upon one another with mutual reproaches.

ayahs.textLatin: Qālū yā wailanā innā kunnā ṭāgīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: [In the end] they said: "Oh, woe unto us! Verily, we did behave outrageously!

ayahs.textArabic: عَسٰى رَبُّنَآ اَنْ يُّبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَآ اِنَّآ اِلٰى رَبِّنَا رٰغِبُوْنَ
ayahs.textLatin: ‘Asā rabbunā ay yubdilanā khairam minhā innā ilā rabbinā rāgibūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: [But] it may be that our Sustainer will grant us something better instead: for, verily, unto our Sustainer do we turn with hope!"

ayahs.textArabic: كَذٰلِكَ الْعَذَابُۗ وَلَعَذَابُ الْاٰخِرَةِ اَكْبَرُۘ لَوْ كَانُوْا يَعْلَمُوْنَ ࣖ
ayahs.textLatin: Każālikal-‘ażāb(u), wa la‘ażābul-ākhirati akbar(u), lau kānū ya‘lamūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: SUCH is the suffering [with which We try some people in this world]; but greater by far will be the suffering [which sinners shall have to bear] in the life to come - if they but knew it!

ayahs.textArabic: اِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِيْنَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنّٰتِ النَّعِيْمِ
ayahs.textEnglish: For, behold, it is the God-conscious [alone] whom gardens of bliss await with their Sustainer:
or should We, perchance, treat those who surrender themselves unto Us as [We would treat] those who remain lost in sin?
What is amiss with you? On what do you base your judgment [of right and wrong]?
Or have you, perchance, a [special] divine writ which you study,
and in which you find all that you may wish to find?

ayahs.textArabic: اَمْ لَكُمْ اَيْمَانٌ عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ اِلٰى يَوْمِ الْقِيٰمَةِۙ اِنَّ لَكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُوْنَۚ
ayahs.textLatin: Am lakum aimānun ‘alainā bāligatun ilā yaumil-qiyāmah(ti), inna lakum lamā taḥkumūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: Or have you received a solemn promise, binding on Us till Resurrection Day, that yours will assuredly be whatever you judge [to be your rightful due]?
Ask them which of them is able to vouch for this!

ayahs.textArabic: اَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَاۤءُۚ فَلْيَأْتُوْا بِشُرَكَاۤىِٕهِمْ اِنْ كَانُوْا صٰدِقِيْنَ
ayahs.textLatin: Am lahum syurakā'(u), falya'tū bisyurakā'ihim in kānū ṣādiqīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: Or have they, perchance, any sages to support their views? Well, then, if they are sincere in this their claim, let them produce those supporters of theirs

ayahs.textArabic: يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ وَّيُدْعَوْنَ اِلَى السُّجُوْدِ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيْعُوْنَۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Yauma yuksyafu ‘an sāqiw wa yud‘auna ilas-sujūdi falā yastaṭī‘ūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: on the Day when man's very being shall be bared to the bone, and when they [who now deny the truth] shall be called upon to prostrate themselves [before God], and shall be unable to do so:

ayahs.textArabic: خَاشِعَةً اَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ  ۗوَقَدْ كَانُوْا يُدْعَوْنَ اِلَى السُّجُوْدِ وَهُمْ سٰلِمُوْنَ
ayahs.textLatin: Khāsyi‘atan abṣāruhum tarhaquhum żillah(tun), wa qad kānū yud‘auna ilas-sujūdi wa hum sālimun(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: downcast will be their eyes, with ignominy overwhelming them - seeing that they had been called upon [in vain] to prostrate themselves [before Him] while they were yet sound [and alive].

ayahs.textArabic: فَذَرْنِيْ وَمَنْ يُّكَذِّبُ بِهٰذَا الْحَدِيْثِۗ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِّنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُوْنَۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Fażarnī wa may yukażżibu bihāżal-ḥadīṡi sanastadrijuhum min ḥaiṡu lā ya‘lamūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: Hence, leave Me alone with such as give the lie to this tiding. We shall bring them low, step by step, without their perceiving how it has come about:

ayahs.textLatin: Wa umlī lahum, inna kaidī matīn(un).
ayahs.textEnglish: for, behold, though I may give them rein for a while, My subtle scheme is exceedingly firm!

ayahs.textArabic: اَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ اَجْرًا فَهُمْ مِّنْ مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُوْنَۚ
ayahs.textLatin: Am tas'aluhum ajran fahum mim magramim muṡqalūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: Or is it that [they fear lest] thou ask them for a reward, [O Prophet,] so that they would be burdened with debt [if they listened to thee]?
Or [do they think] that the hidden reality [of all that exists] is within their grasp, so that [in time] they can write it down?

ayahs.textArabic: فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُنْ كَصَاحِبِ الْحُوْتِۘ اِذْ نَادٰى وَهُوَ مَكْظُوْمٌۗ
ayahs.textLatin: Faṣbir liḥukmi rabbika wa lā takun kaṣāḥibil-ḥūt(i), iż nādā wa huwa makẓūm(un).
ayahs.textEnglish: BEAR THEN with patience thy Sustainer's will and be not like him of the great fish, who cried out [in distress] after having given in to anger.

ayahs.textArabic: لَوْلَآ اَنْ تَدٰرَكَهٗ نِعْمَةٌ مِّنْ رَّبِّهٖ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَرَاۤءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُوْمٌ
ayahs.textLatin: Lau lā an tadārakahū ni‘matum mir rabbihī lanubiża bil-‘arā'i wa huwa mażmūm(un).
ayahs.textEnglish: [And remember:] had not grace from his Sustainer reached him, he would indeed have been cast forth upon that barren shore in a state of disgrace:
but [as it was,] his Sustainer had elected him and placed him among the righteous.

ayahs.textArabic: وَاِنْ يَّكَادُ الَّذِيْنَ كَفَرُوْا لَيُزْلِقُوْنَكَ بِاَبْصَارِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا الذِّكْرَ وَيَقُوْلُوْنَ اِنَّهٗ لَمَجْنُوْنٌ ۘ
ayahs.textLatin: Wa iy yakādul-lażīna kafarū layuzliqūnaka bi'abṣārihim lammā sami‘uż żikra wa yaqūlūna innahū lamajnūn(un).
ayahs.textEnglish: Hence, [be patient,] even though they who are bent on denying the truth would all but kill thee with their eyes whenever they hear this reminder, and [though] they say, "[As for Muhammad,] behold, most surely he is a madman!"

ayahs.textLatin: Wa mā huwa illā żikrul lil-‘ālamīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: [Be patient:] for this is nought else but a reminder [from God] to all mankind.
